note: The draw: which cases were labelled, out of what population, at what sampling fraction. This is label-align.py --sample's INPUT, not only provenance -- re-deriving strata from (split, verdict) weights the held-out tranche against the whole test split, and a grade set that moves after the draw can no longer reconstruct which stratum a case came from. Cut against CAPTURE #1 (responses-0.4.0-a) deliberately: it carries ZERO answer-key reads (2/259 tainted, 1%), while capture #2 has a fatal answer-key read at case 146. Do not relabel these ids against responses-0.4.0-b -- the two captures disagree on 44 of 258 cases (17.1% run-to-run flip rate), so a label taken against one capture does not describe the other. Cut with --held-out-from 213, the batch-6 floor pinned in evals/splits/request-plan.json in the same edit that appended the tranche; the tranche is taken WHOLE (23 of 23) because sampling within a one-shot held-out measurement wastes it. This draw was cut BEFORE any label existed; the pass it enabled has since been completed. Its partner is evals/labels/request-plan-0.4.0-human.jsonl (60 rows: 41 pass, 18 fail, 1 defer at case 157), and evals/findings/request-plan-0.4.0.md now carries the label-derived figures: corrected 85% CI [81,91], TPR 92%, TNR 100% on 18 human negatives; held-out corrected 83% CI [70,100], TNR 100% on 4. label-align.py reads THIS file for the strata -- the weights below are inputs to those numbers, not a record of them, so the two files must be committed together or the rate becomes unreconstructable.
